candidates.name: Cancellation eligibility classifier
candidates.runtime_observation: Reservation cabin, creation time, insurance, itinerary flight statuses, user membership, and the user's cancellation reason.
candidates.decision_variable: Whether any segment has flown and whether at least one native policy eligibility condition holds.
possible_runtime_states: z1: an itinerary segment has landed or is flying
z2: no segment has flown and an eligibility condition holds
z3: no segment has flown and no eligibility condition holds

correct_behavior.z1: Do not cancel; transfer because the Agent cannot handle a partially flown itinerary.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: The user's assertion is not authoritative; the reservation and flight-instance states must be read at runtime.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Collect authoritative state, apply the flown-segment hard gate first, then evaluate the independent eligibility predicates, and map the classified case to transfer, cancel, or deny.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: The tool itself accepts ineligible cancellations, so a caller can over-trust the write API or overlook one of several disjunctive eligibility paths.
candidates.information_boundary: All branch inputs are available from normal user interaction and Airline read tools; the branch label remains construction-only.

candidates.name: Constrained flight-candidate selection
candidates.runtime_observation: Direct and one-stop search results containing routes, dates, times, seat counts, cabin prices, and connection structure.
candidates.decision_variable: The feasible candidate set after hard constraints, followed by the user's ranking preference and fallback ordering.
possible_runtime_states: z1: preferred feasible candidate exists
z2: preferred candidate is infeasible but a lower-ranked feasible candidate exists
z3: no candidate satisfies the hard constraints

correct_behavior.z2: Propose the next feasible candidate under the declared fallback ordering.
correct_behavior.z3: Do not mutate; report that the constrained request cannot be fulfilled or ask which constraint may change.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: Flight IDs, availability, cabin capacity, prices, and connection timings are returned only by runtime search.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Normalize candidates, apply route/date/chronology/capacity/cabin/budget constraints as hard filters, rank survivors by the user objective, and use an explicit fallback only after proving the preferred class empty.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: A caller can rank before filtering, compare only direct results, ignore connection chronology, or silently relax a hard constraint.
candidates.information_boundary: The chosen flight must be derived from public search results; no gold candidate may enter Agent or Learner context.

candidates.name: Checked-baggage allowance and charge classification
candidates.runtime_observation: Authoritative membership, reservation cabin, passenger count, current bag counts, and requested final bag count.
candidates.decision_variable: The membership-by-cabin allowance multiplied by passenger count, and the requested increment above that allowance/current paid-bag state.
possible_runtime_states: z1: requested final bags remain entirely within the free allowance
z2: requested final bags exceed the free allowance and require payment
z3: the request would remove bags and is policy-ineligible

correct_behavior.z1: Update total bags with the correct nonfree count and no positive charge.
correct_behavior.z2: Compute nonfree bags and the incremental fee, obtain payment and confirmation, then update.
correct_behavior.z3: Deny the removal mutation while preserving existing bags.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: The user may misstate membership or omit cabin and current baggage; authoritative values live in user/reservation state.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Read authoritative inputs, compute per-passenger allowance from the policy matrix, derive total free capacity and incremental nonfree bags, then select free update, paid update, or denial.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: The calculation combines two entities, a policy matrix, passenger cardinality, current state, and incremental rather than total charging.
candidates.information_boundary: Only tool-observed membership/reservation fields and the request are needed; computed oracle totals stay evaluator-only.

candidates.name: Compensation eligibility and amount classifier
candidates.runtime_observation: Membership, insurance, cabin, flight status, passenger count, complaint type, explicit compensation request, and whether a required change/cancellation completed.
candidates.decision_variable: Eligible customer predicate combined with disruption type and remedy state.
possible_runtime_states: z1: cancelled-flight complaint and customer is compensation-eligible
z2: delayed-flight complaint, requested remedy completed, and customer is eligible
z3: ineligible customer, unsupported reason, no explicit request, or delayed remedy not completed

correct_behavior.z1: Offer/send a certificate worth 100 dollars per passenger after required confirmation.
correct_behavior.z2: Offer/send a certificate worth 50 dollars per passenger after the change/cancellation and confirmation.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: Eligibility and disruption facts require profile, reservation, and flight-state reads; delayed compensation also depends on a runtime remedy outcome.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Verify facts, gate on explicit request and customer eligibility, classify disruption and remedy completion, calculate amount by passenger count, otherwise take no compensation action.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: The procedure has ordered prerequisites and mutually different amount/no-action branches; the generic certificate tool enforces none of them.
candidates.information_boundary: All evidence comes from conversation and public tools; eligibility/branch annotations remain hidden.

candidates.name: Flight-versus-cabin modification legality classifier
candidates.runtime_observation: Requested mutation type, current cabin, existing flight identities, and whether any segment has flown.
candidates.decision_variable: Whether the request changes flights, cabin only, or both, combined with basic-economy and flown-state gates.
possible_runtime_states: z1: flight change on basic economy
z2: cabin-only change with no flown segment
z3: cabin change after any segment has flown
z4: permitted flight change preserving itinerary identity

correct_behavior.z1: Do not change flights; a separately requested and permitted cabin-only operation may be considered, but no implicit workaround is authorized.
correct_behavior.z2: After price calculation and confirmation, update the cabin while preserving every flight.
correct_behavior.z4: After availability, payment, and confirmation checks, update the complete flight list.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: Current cabin, exact segments, and flown status must be obtained from reservation and flight state.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Classify the requested delta before applying gates: flight identity changes and cabin-only changes have different eligibility rules; preserve all non-target fields and map each case to update or denial.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: The shared update_reservation_flights API can obscure the semantic difference between a cabin-only write and a flight replacement and does not enforce policy gates.
candidates.information_boundary: The delta is derived from request plus tool-observed current state; construction does not reveal the legal branch.

candidates.name: Agent-selected payment source
candidates.runtime_observation: Saved payment methods, balances, transaction price, and refund/charge direction.
candidates.decision_variable: Which stored payment identifier to pass to a booking or update.
possible_runtime_states: z1: one source can cover the charge
z2: several sources can cover the charge
z3: no permitted source can cover the charge

correct_behavior.z1: Potentially use that source after user confirmation.
correct_behavior.z2: Ask the user to choose unless the user already supplied a preference.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: Balances and exact price require runtime reads/search, but authority to choose among valid methods belongs to the user.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Check type and sufficiency constraints, then request a user choice among remaining methods.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: A caller might choose an arbitrary valid method or use a certificate for an update.
candidates.rejection_reason: Native semantics do not define a unique Agent-selected downstream action when multiple methods are valid; tasks that do define one usually put the preference directly in the user instruction.

candidates.name: Reservation-set temporal and entity consistency resolution
candidates.runtime_observation: The user's reservation IDs followed by each itinerary's times, airports, dates, and passengers.
candidates.decision_variable: Which reservations involving the user are mutually inconsistent with fixed location/time commitments and are eligible for the requested correction.
possible_runtime_states: z1: reservation is consistent or belongs only to another passenger
z2: reservation conflicts with an authoritative time/location commitment and may be corrected
z3: reservation conflicts but the requested mutation is policy-ineligible

correct_behavior.z2: Propose the minimal correction for that reservation, then mutate only after confirmation.
correct_behavior.z3: Preserve it and explain/transfer according to the applicable operation policy.

candidates.why_not_known_at_start: The user supplies identity and commitments but the complete candidate reservation set and itinerary graph are obtained from runtime tools.
candidates.potential_reusable_procedure: Enumerate only the user's relevant itineraries, construct chronological location constraints, exclude other-passenger records, identify conflicts, then apply operation eligibility and minimal-change selection.
candidates.why_base_might_fail: The decision requires cross-object temporal reasoning, entity scoping, and a minimal-change rule rather than matching one field.
candidates.information_boundary: All graph inputs are observable; gold conflicting reservation IDs must remain evaluator-only.

recommended_for_pilot.reason: The runtime candidate set and action binding are explicit, surface variants are abundant, the procedure is medium-level rather than an answer, and final itinerary state is semantically evaluable.

It provides a clean multi-state legal-operation classifier with native evidence reads and distinct cancel/deny/transfer consequences, though later calibration must test whether the visible policy makes it too easy.
